{{verse|chapter=7|verse=31|align=float}}† {{outside L|The Go{{ls}}pel vpō the 11 Sunday after Penteco{{ls}}t.}}And againe going out of the coa{{ls}}tes {{outside R|''`of Tyre and Sidon, he came''}}`of Tyre, he came by Sidon' to the {{ls}}ea of Galilee through the middes of the coa{{ls}}tes of Decapolis. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=32|align=float}}† And they bring to him one deafe and dumme: and they be{{ls}}ought him that he vvould impo{{ls}}e his hand vpon him. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=33|align=float}}† And taking him from the multitude apart, he put his fingers into his eares: and {{sup|‖}} {{ls}}pitting, touched his tongue. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=34|align=float}}† and looking vp vnto heauen, he groned, and {{ls}}aid to him, ''{{sup|‖}} Ephphetha'', vvhich is, ''Be thou opened''. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=35|align=float}}† And immediatly his eares vvere opened, and the {{ls}}tring of his tongue vvas loo{{ls}}ed, and he {{ls}}pake right. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=36|align=float}}† And he commaunded them not to tel any body. ''2. Common.''] Common and vncleane is al one. For the Iewes were commaunded by the Law to eate certaine kindes of meates only, and not al indifferently: and becau{{ls}}e the{{ls}}e were {{ls}}eparated from other meates, and as it were {{ls}}anctified to their v{{ls}}e, they called the other common and profane: and becau{{ls}}e the Law calleth tho{{ls}}e cleane and the{{ls}}e vncleane, thereof it is, that vncleane and common is al one. as in this Chapter often, and ''Act. 10''.

''7. Precepts of men.''] {{outside L|Commaundements of men.}}Mens ordinances which be repugnant to Gods commaundements, be here condemned: as al ob{{ls}}eruations not edifying nor profitable to the fulfilling of Gods commaundements, be vaine and {{ls}}uperfluous: as many ob{{ls}}eruations of the Phari{{ls}}ees were then, and the like traditions of Heretikes be now. for how{{ls}}oeuer they bragge of Scriptures, al their maner of admini{{ls}}tration and mini{{ls}}terie is their owne tradition and inuention without al Scripture and warrant of Gods word. {{outside L|Traditions.}}But the traditions of the Apo{{ls}}tles and Ancients, and al the precepts of holy Church we are commaunded to keepe, as things not pre{{ls}}cribed by man, but by the Holy Gho{{ls}}t. ''Act. 15, 28. 41. 2 The{{ls}}{{ls}}al. 2, 15''.

''11. Gift.''] To giue to the Church or Altar is not forbidden, {{outside L|Dutie to parēts.}}but the for{{ls}}aking of a mans parents in their nece{{ls}}{{ls}}itie, pretending or excu{{ls}}ing the matter vpon his giuing that which {{ls}}hould relieue them, to God or to the Altar, that is impious and vnnatural. And the{{ls}}e Phari{{ls}}ees teaching children {{ls}}o to neglect their duties to their parents, did wickedly.

''15. Nothing entering into a man.''] As the{{ls}}e wordes of our Sauiour do not import, that the Iewes then might haue eaten of tho{{ls}}e meates which God forbade them: no more doe they now, that we Chri{{ls}}tians may eate of meates which the Church forbiddeth vs. {{outside L|Ab{{ls}}tinēce from certaine meates.}}And yet both then and now al meates are cleane, and nothing entering into a man, defileth a man. For neither they then, nor we now ab{{ls}}teine, for that any meates are of their nature abominable, or defile the eaters, but they for {{ls}}ignification, we for obedience and cha{{ls}}ti{{ls}}ement of our bodies.
